items.title: Nodusfall Accused of Being an Elden Ring Rip-Off
Genshin Impact devs' new action game Nodusfall feels like Elden Ring Nightreign at home, but don't write it off yet
items.summary: Going hands-on with Nodusfall at Gamescom 2026
items.content:
Gaming Genshin Impact devs' new action game Nodusfall feels like Elden Ring Nightreign at home, but don't write it off yet GamesRadar+ Follow Catherine Lewis Wed, September 2, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC Wed, September 2, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.

Nodusfall does not look like your typical Hoyoverse game. Distinctly lacking in bright colors and bubbly anime-style characters, it's hard to believe that this gloomy, intense PvE action game comes from the same studio behind Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail. But after a brief hands-on session with the game, I'm already eager to dive back in for more.

It might not look like a Hoyoverse game, but there's one thing Nodusfall certainly does look like. Namely Elden Ring , and by extension, its co-op sibling Nightreign . This doesn't end with its reveal trailer vibes – we have a summonable Torrent-like steed who can be called with a very familiar-sounding whistle, a character who can transform into a phase two Malenia lookalike with massive, crusty wings, Estus flask-like healing potions, and bonfires to rest at.

Developer: MiHoYo Platfom(s): PC Release date: TBC

Needless to say, it's hard not to draw comparisons – 'we've got Elden Ring Nightreign at home,' my brain screams. However, while teaming up with other players to take down big bosses might evoke feelings of FromSoftware's co-op title, there's a big difference with Nodusfall: it's not nearly as hard. This can be considered a blessing or a curse depending on where you stand on Soulslike difficulty. As a fan of the genre, I still found myself having plenty of fun taking down the three bosses in my hands-on session, including an enormous dragon and Qiongqi (a horned and winged tiger-like beast from Chinese mythology), but my victories definitely didn't come with the same level of satisfaction as they might have had they been slightly harder won. I can't recall falling in battle even once, largely thanks to what felt like an unlimited supply of heals.

To be fair, this factor may also have been helped by one of the playable characters being a dedicated healer, who I choose to play in my session. I have strong magic attacks up my sleeve, from small projectiles to ice-powered strikes and an enormous laser beam move, but my main contribution to my team comes in the form of my healing abilities. I can choose to lock onto a specific ally to unleash a steady flow of health restoration, not unlike Mercy's Caduceus staff in Overwatch, or heal multiple teammates around me at once in a smaller burst.

The specific ally lock-on heal can feel a little clunky at times – there were more than a few times where I assisted someone who definitely didn't need it because they were awkwardly stood in front of someone else who desperately needed my help. Comparing directly to Elden Ring Nightreign, though, it's really cool to have a healer option in the first place. Again, it seems that Nodusfall doesn't come close to being as challenging as FromSoftware's Soulslikes to begin with, but having a medic role like this is no doubt going to provide a welcome option to players who aren't as comfortable with getting up close and personal on the frontlines of a brutal battle. I always tend to gravitate towards support classes in games – there's just something so satisfying about keeping your friends and allies going – so I'm pleased to be allowed that here.

I'd have been curious to try out the other playable characters to get a greater feel for Nodusfall's combat. What I experienced was fun, but my attacks felt like they were lacking weight, leaving me craving just a tad more oomph. You really can't fault the boss battles when it comes to how cinematic they are, though – my team and I tore through multiple phases in each fight, with our final battle against the Maldrake dragon evolving after the knight riding on its back dismounted their steed and began attacking us from the ground, forcing us to split our forces to take on two enemies at once.

The concept of an easier, more accessible co-op action game like Nightreign is bound to be appealing

Though my Nodusfall experience was limited to co-op PvE, Hoyoverse has clarified that PvP and PvPvE modes are also planned for the long term, and that you'll also be able to enjoy most of the core content solo. From what I played, though, it'd be a shame to do so since you'd miss out on the flashy Joint Execution moves – who doesn't want to team up to drive a massive greatsword through a beast's head?

I was also pleased to learn that, despite plans to make Nodusfall a free-to-play game, playable characters won't be locked behind a gacha system. With that said, the devs are considering monetizing cosmetics, and I can't say I'm surprised. While kitting out my healer girl with a new outfit, various accessories including a fancy, glowing cape were screaming microtransaction potential. I can't say I love that aspect, but I'd certainly much rather the monetization be incorporated here than the core gameplay.

As someone who loved Elden Ring Nightreign, I suppose it's only natural that I'd enjoy Nodusfall. Its vibe is very similar, but I'm very curious to see where Hoyoverse takes it from here. The concept of an easier, more accessible co-op action game like Nightreign is bound to be appealing to many, and could be a bridge for those who find FromSoftware's games a bit too difficult. Regardless, there's something in here that's got me craving more – but for now, I guess I've literally got Nightreign at home.

Nodusfall isn't a gacha game, Mihoyo confirms, because unlike Genshin Impact you'll unlock characters "through continued play" instead

items.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Could Be My Favorite Action Game Since Elden Ring, And There’s A Preorder Deal
Four Years Later, Players Are Still Falling For Elden Ring’s Biggest Trick
items.summary: New Elden Ring players are swiftly being transported to Sellia Crystal Tunnel and learning about the game the hard way.
items.content:
Four Years Later, Players Are Still Falling For Elden Ring’s Biggest Trick From TheGamer (Written by Sam Woods) on September 1, 2026 | OpenCritic

Elden Ring is made by FromSoftware. FromSoftware makes notoriously difficult video games. Therefore, in conclusion, Elden Ring is a difficult video game. This is something many of us have found out by now, with the masterpiece having been released over four and a half years ago.

However, good games never die, and with Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition now releasing on the Nintendo Switch 2, a whole new audience is experiencing the game. It also means a whole new audience is experiencing the trials and tribulations that come with it. One of these, which many of us are all too familiar with, is the Teleporter Trap in the Dragon Burnt Ruins, something that new players are encountering for the first time, with hilarious consequences.

Elden Ring is FromSoftware's first big open-world game. The way the map is laid out, however, means players are likely to gravitate towards the Dragon Burnt Ruins pretty early on in their adventures. It's a grand introduction to the game's mechanics, enemies, and structure, but it has one little caveat — a Teleporter Trap that will transport you into the far more dangerous Sellia Crystal Tunnel .

It's a trap that's easy to fall into, simply by opening...

items.title: The path to becoming Elden Lord has begun!
items.content:
ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition is now available for the Nintendo Switch 2 system! This version of the game also includes the expansion, ‘Shadow of the Erdtree’, additional armour, and custom skins for Torrent, your spectral steed.

Unravel the mysteries of the Elden Ring’s power. Encounter adversaries with profound backgrounds, characters with their own unique motivations for helping or hindering your progress, and fearsome creatures.

Guided by grace, brandish the power of the Elden Ring and become an Elden Lord in the Lands Between.

Below, you can find out more about the perilous journey ahead. And if you keep scrolling, we’ve also gathered five quick tips that could help you stay alive.

Journey through the Lands Between, a fantasy world from Hidetaka Miyazaki, creator of the influential DARK SOULS video game series, and best-selling fantasy author, George R. R. Martin.

Traverse the breathtaking world on foot or on horseback, alone or online* with other players, and fully immerse yourself in the grassy plains, suffocating swamps, spiralling mountains, foreboding castles and other sites of grandeur.

Create your character and define your playstyle by experimenting with a wide variety of weapons, magical abilities, and skills found throughout the world.

While playing online, Furlcalling Finger Remedy can reveal golden co-op multiplayer* signs. Whether you’re trying to take on normal enemies, bosses, or invaders, you can touch golden signs to summon up to two other players into your world for assistance.

Using a Tarnished’s Furled Finger creates a summon sign that allows other online players* to call you into their worlds. While it’s great to lend a helping hand, this can also be a useful tool to learn about bosses or farm Runes.

If you strategically move behind an enemy and hit your attack, this will cause you to backstab them. Backstabs are a great way to quickly eliminate an enemy or deal a significant chunk of damage to them.

Some NPCs can be a little chatty—which is a good thing! Going through their dialogue can reveal more about the world and what to watch out for.

You may notice a golden ray reaching out after touching a Site of Grace. This Guidance of Grace points you towards a path that advances the main story. This means that you can get lost in exploration whenever you’d like, but the Guidance of Grace will always direct you back to your main objective: becoming Elden Lord.

There is no easy path to becoming Elden Lord. Remember that every death can be a lesson to build your own skills. While it may be difficult at times, the sense of accomplishment can be incredibly rewarding, especially as you unravel a little more of the vast world’s mysteries.

If you’d like to learn more about the game or make a purchase, please check out the link below.

items.title: Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition is exciting enough on its own, but it's also our last chance to properly experience the game's launch day hype
items.content:
One last hurrah for "fort comma night," "Mist, or Beast," and "offer pickle."

You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday.

Elden Ring is one of the best videogames I've ever played, and now, four years from launch, is possibly the last time you'll get to experience it as an event . The Tarnished Edition DLC looks small on paper⁠—two new classes and a smattering of armor and items⁠—but it is still something new, something unexpected added to our 2022 game of the year.

What in any other context might make for a Horse Armor -style embarrassment is one of the most exciting releases of 2026 for me, and I'm only, like, a quarter joking. Elden Ring is the type of game that made a couple borked quests getting patched into a massive communal treasure hunt . New weapons, armor, and classes at this late date feels like a profound gift, even if I'm paying for the privilege.

But, in addition to the material additions coming to Elden Ring, the Tarnished Edition DLC serves as an enticement to the playerbase, something to bring them back all at one time and bring life back to the Lands Between's ailing multiplayer invasions and co-operative boss battling.

I still remember how magical the first days of Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree were, the density of asynchronous messages and ease of matchmaking. The Tarnished Edition won't be able to match either of those highs, but its launch may represent the biggest spike in player activity we could ever expect to see in Elden Ring again.

If you've somehow missed the boat on this one since 2022, I envy the first experience you're about to have. Elden Ring's fantasy is somehow both mythic and anthropological, zoomed out, and deeply personal.

Elden Ring players are hard at work putting the new Tarnished Edition DLC's gear to the test Where to find new armor and weapons in Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition This action RPG's more-with-more-on-top excess is as fun as expansion design gets

You're an anonymous warrior on a quest to become God's Husband (gender-agnostic). The God in question is a man and woman, separate but the same, consubstantial with, and plotting against themselves. Her pope is a giant turtle , and she is perpetuating a millennia-old conflict involving both racial animus and metaphysics. You can make her goth half- (single? step?) daughter God instead if you so choose.

It's all set in a world of literally impossible beauty, one of the best fantasy settings ever rendered in a videogame. It's dominated by the alien, iconic view of the Erdtree, an ethereal, skyscraper-sized growth that's visible from every part of the Lands Between. Elden Ring is, perhaps, one of FromSoftware 's most bright and cheerful creations to date, but it's also one of the weirdest. In four years, it's lodged itself into my psyche like almost no game world I've ever seen.

But enough about all that nerd stuff: FromSoft had already ruined all other 3D action games for me by the time Elden Ring came out, and while it lacks the pure focus of Sekiro's perfect block symphony , I think it matches that more straightforward action game as a fantasy combat experience. Elden Ring is one of the broadest, deepest, and most exquisitely designed action-RPGs that's ever been made.

It even contains Sekiro in a limited sense: One of the character build options added in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is a perfect block mechanic lifted straight out of the ninja sim. Like no other game I've played, Elden Ring balances mechanically pure "it's your fault if you die" combat with a myriad of class fantasies and character build options. Knights, barbarians, spellcasters, rogues, priests, samurai, nude men with earthenware hats, you can inhabit any of these roles while engaging in some of the tightest, richest, and most challenging action combat put to silicon.

items.title: Afraid to start Elden Ring? Nintendo has prepared a special guide
items.summary: Nintendo has released an official guide for beginners playing Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on Switch 2, introducing newcomers to the basics of traversing the Lands Between.
items.content:
1 Источник: YouTube-канал Nintendo of America 30 August 2026, 11:15 Dmitry Krivov Nintendo has released an official guide for beginners playing Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on Switch 2, introducing newcomers to the basics of traversing the Lands Between.

The release of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 took place on August 28, 2026. For this event, Nintendo and Bandai Namco prepared a short video with basic tips for those new to a FromSoftware game. The guide explains the core principles of Elden Ring and tells what to expect during the journey through the Lands Between. The player's main goal is to explore the world, collect the shards of the shattered Elden Ring, and ultimately become the Elden Lord.

Tarnished Edition includes the main game and the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. The edition also received new content: starting classes Idus Knight and Heavy Knight, new weapons and equipment, and the ability to change Torrent's appearance. Some of the content is available to owners of the game on other platforms via the paid Tarnished Pack.

Initial reviews indicate that the Switch 2 version turned out technically much better than early demonstrations showed.

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

The following elements will be added upon purchase of the "Tarnished Pack" DLC.

  • Added Idus Knight and Heavy Knight as new starting classes, selectable during character creation. Note: The equipment of each new starting class can also be obtained by purchasing it from merchants in the Lands Between or by finding it in the world.

items.title: I Tested Elden Ring On Switch 2 In A Cozy Cafe And It Ran Just Fine, Which Is Great News For A Remarkable Game
items.summary: You shouldn't play it in the rain/but you can play it on a train
items.content:
Elden Ring is an excellent, excellent video game. It’s got that smashy FromSoftware combat, a couple hundred boss fights that are all (mostly) unique and fun, character build customization for miles, a gorgeous and massive open world that’s a treat to explore, an intriguing story and hidden secrets, and a robust DLC that could be a game all its own. There’s a reason (well, many reasons!) why it’s almost universally critically acclaimed and still beloved by fans a few years after launch, too.

I love Elden Ring ! But when Ethan asked me to take on the review of the Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2, I wasn’t, like, stoked about it. I beat Elden Ring back when it first came out, easily dumping over 100 hours into the main game and probably another solid 40 or more into the DLC. And I played the Tarnished Edition at a preview event earlier this year for about 20 minutes, after which time I told everyone I spoke with about the experience that yup, that was Elden Ring all right! Elden Ring on a Switch 2! Game’s great, but I don’t necessarily need to play it again. What else is there to say?

It turns out, after playing for review, I do have one additional thing to say: Elden Ring is, apparently, pretty fun to play in public. Ideally at a cozy coffee shop with squoshy chairs where you can purchase hot London fogs to drink while you play.

Elden Ring was technically playable on the go before the Tarnished Edition , for folks with a Steam Deck. I have one of those, but the device, unlike the Switch 2, is not fun to take out in public. It’s heavy to hold, does not have a convenient kickstand, and you have to hold it in your hands to play if you don’t want to drag a controller around too. With the Switch 2, I could set the console on the table with the kickstand out, take the Joy-Cons off, lean back in my chair, and play Elden Ring while soothing cafe music played in the background. Every time I die (which is often), I get a nice sip of tea. I do not rage. I do not tense up. Helpfully, the cat (who is not here in the cafe with me) does not butt her head against the triggers and cause me to swing my sword randomly. Life is good.

In basically every other respect, I stick to my guns from the preview: this is Elden Ring ! It’s on the Switch 2 now! There were concerns after the first round of early previews that it ran poorly, but those were fixed by the time I previewed it earlier this year and remain fixed now. It runs fine. There are still occasional little framerate drops and yeah, it doesn’t look quite as nice as it will on your PS5 or Xbox Series, but who cares? It still plays great. The minor technical compromises didn’t interfere with combat in any way that was meaningful to me. It still looks good. It’s still lovely to stand on a cliff’s edge and look out in the direction of the Erdtree, the sun’s rays glistening through the clouds and a skyline of crumbling ruin all around.

I should mention that the Tarnished Edition does not have any meaningful new features. There are four new armor sets, a bit of customization for Torrent, and two new starting classes. Unfortunately, two of those new armor sets are starting sets for the two new classes, Heavy Knight and Idus Knight. I played as the Idus Knight and replaced my armor almost immediately with some tunic thing I got off a knight in the very first part of Limgrave, because it had better stats. I think I wore this same tunic when I played the game the first time. Shame, because the new starting armor genuinely looked great. I found the addition of these two new classes to be extremely whatever: you’re going to customize all your stats and replace all your gear almost immediately anyway. The Idus Knight was just a Samurai two levels lower, with different equipment. These additions did nothing for me, and certainly will do nothing for anyone after the first hour of game.

This release does include the superb Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, bundled right in from the start, though. That rules.

But who cares? It’s Elden Ring , on Switch 2! I can easily play it on a plane or on a train, in a box or with a fox, here or there, anywhere! I can take it to bars, to rooftop wine parties. I can play it outside on a patio with a cold one in a koozie next to me as the summer sun sets. I recognize that this is just effectively restating the main gimmick of the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, but I admittedly haven’t taken my Switch 2 out much since it launched last year. Elden Ring , the best game of 2022 and arguably one of the best games of the decade, is a great excuse to do so. Give it a shot. Order yourself a latte or, a little later in the day, maybe a nice glass of pinot noir, bust out your Switch 2, and give it a shot.

This article was corrected post-publication: Limveld is Nightreign , Limgrave is Elden Ring . I can never keep them straight.

Image: FromSoftware/Bandai Namco Elden Ring Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 3 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap So you've defeated Radagon and the Elden Beast to become an Elden Lord. Maybe you're sick of getting killed by Malenia and need something that will help you get back into the fray. Perhaps you're looking to get back into the swing of things ahead of Elden Ring 's release on Nintendo Switch 2 . Whatever the reason, you want to make The Lands Between exciting again. Here are some tried and true ways to reinvent FromSoftware's lauded open-world RPG.

Let's start with the easiest thing you can do: Play Elden Ring again . After you reach an ending, the game will ask you if you want to begin Journey 2. If you select yes, you'll start over at the Chapel of Anticipation with the boss that's designed to kill you. In New Game Plus, you'll keep your Runes, level, most of your inventory and key items, as well as however much of the map you uncovered previously. While this means you'll begin the game with a number of enhancements, the game also increases the health, attack power, and Rune rewards for all bosses. Bosses will drop duplicates of weapons you already have, allowing you to dual-wield combinations that would be impossible in the base game.

Why make a notoriously difficult game even harder? Well, it's one way to appreciate the game's incredible boss battles. The version of the boss you defeated the first time is not that enemy's final form. If beating bosses the first time was a thrill, imagine what it'll feel like when those villains pull out all the stops? You can begin as many new Journeys as you'd like, but Elden Ring stops upping the ante after your eighth re-run.

Elden Ring is an entirely different beast online. Here, you'll meet all sorts of characters, from alien-looking Albinaurics who wield ridiculous weapons like trumpets, to half-naked men who wear jars on their heads . Trying co-op or PvP is worth it just to get a taste of that circus. You may get some new build ideas, or find a low-stakes way to try out a new tactic.

PvP also allows you to get a better sense of how good you truly are at the game. It's one thing to defeat a boss with a specific set of moves and another to kill a live player who is capable of anything. If you win, you'll get a Rune Arc — powerful items that are scarce in the base game.

You can also get Rune Arcs from doing co-op play, which some people may prefer over the intensity of PvP. You can invite other players into your game to help you with a tough section, or you can lend a hand to those in need. Some people like to crack a Finger item during sections of the game they've already mastered. These portions of the game may not pose a challenge anymore, but they'll make you feel like a hero on par with Let Me Solo Her . You could also be a total jerk to other players. We don't recommend trolling, but you should go in to multiplayer expecting it.

A player with an Rivers of Blood and Uchigatana Image: From Software via Polygon Elden Ring packs a number of different classes and a large assortment of unique equipment that will immediately make the game feel like a new experience. Wielding the Meteorite Staff, for example, is very different than running a bleed build with Rivers of Blood or Moonveil. Better yet, you don't have to start a new playthrough to muck around and see what you like. With Larval Tears, you can respec at any time after beating Rennala in the Raya Lucaria.

If you're really itching for a challenge, you can always try progressing through the game as a Wretch — a class that begins with no armor and a wooden club for a weapon. Though this class is tough to play at first, its evenly distributed stats make it more of a blank canvas for whatever hare-brained build you want to try.

Even after a number of updates, some classes are stronger than others. The Incantation-focused Prophet can be difficult to figure out until you find the right spells. By that same token, progressing as a Prophet may feel all the more rewarding. Those of you picking up the Switch 2 Tarnished Edition of the game will be pleased to know it comes with two totally new classes, the Heavy Knight and Idus Knight. You could be one of the first Elden Ring players to figure out how to best use these new options!

Image: FromSoftware/Bandai Namco Alex Garland's film adaptation of the game is coming up , so it may not be a bad time to revisit Elden Ring 's story. Much of the reason people are obsessed with FromSoftware games is the cryptic but rich lore, which in this case, was written with the help of George R.R. Martin. The politics of The Lands Between are surprisingly complicated, and characters may be connected in ways that are not immediately obvious . It's fun to interpret all the item descriptions and then compare your findings to popular fan theories about the game. One could easily spend dozens of hours watching recap videos or explainers on all the things Elden Ring never spells out.

Another aspect to sink your teeth into is all the data-mined videos that show early gameplay ideas, cut content , and storylines that feel like they should have been included in the actual game. Two cut questlines involving Kale and the Silver Tear enemies in the Eternal Cit will get you cursing at what could have been. Before you know it, you'll find yourself arguing with a 3-year-old Reddit post about what one unused voice line actually means.

Image: FromSoftware/Bandai Namco Unless you're playing the Switch 2 enhanced port of Elden Ring , you're going to need to spend some extra money to play the DLC. But if Elden Ring is excellent, Shadow of the Erdtree is incredible. Ideas and storylines that didn't get fully fleshed out in the base game are explored to their fullest extent in the DLC, particularly when it comes to Miquella. Miquella is responsible for many of the base game's events — but we never see the Empyrian in the game.

It's a hefty addition to the game that's packed with all sorts of show-stopping bosses that will impress and anger you in equal measure. Be warned: Shadow of the Erdtree is significantly more difficult than Elden Ring . Most people get stuck on SotE's first boss for a few hours even if they're overleveled for the base game.

items.title: What it's like beating Elden Ring twice a week for 4 years: "I think it's the greatest game that's ever been made"
items.content:
Playing FromSoftware's best RPG for a living takes you to some weird places

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Bandai Namco) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter FromSoftware is in a curious position. It released Elden Ring, its most successful and arguably best game, and ever since has exclusively released games that are very different to Elden Ring. And yes, that does include Elden Ring Nightreign, an experimental spinoff that cleverly reuses some assets and shrinks the world, then builds a PvE battle royale experience around it.

We've had Armored Core 6 and we've got The Duskbloods coming, but FromSoftware hasn't announced a new single-player dark fantasy RPG of the kind it's known for. This has left many fans revisiting the RPGs FromSoft has already released, most especially Elden Ring and its gargantuan world and DLC. It's hard to think of anybody who has gotten more out of Elden Ring than Bushy, a challenge runner who's beaten this famously long and difficult RPG over 400 times by his best estimate.

On Twitch and YouTube , Bushy is known for completing challenge runs in Elden Ring, and occasionally other games, that put restrictions on how he plays. Across hundreds of clears, he's amassed a huge collection of absurd rule sets. You have the classics, like one-hitting bosses, never dying, never getting hit, always getting hit, or kicking enemies to death. Mods, some of them commissioned by Bushy just for this purpose, also allow for stranger runs with teleportation, mismatched areas and enemies, or randomized items. Then we get to the truly specific stuff, like his most recent video: " Elden Ring But I Can Only Use White Items ".

It was this color-specific video series that pushed me to reach out to Bushy. Man , I thought, this guy has done everything . And it's easy to think that Bushy must be running out of ideas or growing sick of the game by now, but he tells me he's every bit as in love with Elden Ring as he has been for the past "3,500 to 4,000" hours of game time.

"I think it's the greatest game that's ever been made," Bushy says. "I always just have a ton of fun with it. If I didn't have that much fun with it, I wouldn't still be trying to come up with new, inventive ways to beat it. Don't get me wrong, part of that is absolutely that it's my job, and there are external forces that are encouraging me to play Elden Ring. But I think it's honestly more of a blessing than it is a curse."

7 years ago, the first Elden Ring trailer changed my life Elden Ring on Switch 2 might be my new go-to version of the action-RPG from now on Dark Souls isn't "an especially difficult game," former Tekken boss says The release of Elden Ring Nightreign did give Bushy some space to play another game, and the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC was a refreshing injection of new content and items, but he always comes back to the game.

He considers the pessimistic read of his position. "You could look at that in a negative light," he says. "You're playing Elden Ring because you have to, because it's the only thing that makes you money. But that's not really how I look at it. Elden Ring is a game that is big enough, massive enough, deep enough, that has such a breadth of content, that having motivation and a reason to actually play it that much is really quite the blessing. I get to play it a whole lot more than other people do."

Bushy's putting every last grain of Elden Ring under the magnifying glass. Like a speedrunner, he talks about individual bosses as things to "practice". His videos often see him deliberately rotate through spells, weapons, and items in order to explain and engage with multiple parts of the game rather than simply using the first winning option he can find, and his rule sets regularly lead to interesting discoveries about overlooked items and strategies. I'm reminded of MMO players running self-sufficient accounts, whose self-imposed challenges force them to play the game in novel ways.

His favorite challenge runs are those that dramatically change the game and are "higher effort" overall, like the one where he was teleported to a random checkpoint every five minutes. He also played the game with an aggression mod that made every enemy follow and attack him at all times, with basically no way to lose or avoid aggro. It didn't go well.

Now, Bushy can just throw out obscene sentences like this: "I've on average beaten the game probably twice a week since the game came out." This schedule wasn't immovable, but his channel history bears it out. I've learned not to underestimate FromSoftware fans, but I certainly haven't met anyone else who's rolled credits this many times. Additionally, Bushy says, "the longest I've gone not playing Elden Ring since it came out has probably been like three weeks."

Bushy is certainly looking forward to future FromSoftware games, but somehow reckons he's got more than enough Elden Ring challenge run ideas left in the tank. When he started playing the game for a living, building on years of streaming other games, he was "hopeful" after his early challenges got some attention. "I made lots of very bad videos and got more views than I had ever gotten at the time," he recalls. Elden Ring's massive audience was enough to turn the game into a career for him, not unlike how creators like VaatiVidya make a living by interpreting FromSoftware lore.

"I still want to do them," Bushy says of his challenge runs. "Simply because it's cool to talk about all of the unique interactions that I can find with specific weapon types and what I think they're strong at, what I think they're weak at, and share the experience that I have in this game with the people that are interested in it. As long as people are interested, I'm more than happy to do it."

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE

items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: ELDEN RING: SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE – Official Vinyl Soundtrack
items.summary: Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree. Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set
items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.
